import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Erdős Problem 867

*References:*
- [erdosproblems.com/867](https://www.erdosproblems.com/867)
- [CoPh96] Coppersmith, Don and Phillips, Steven, *On a question of Erdős on subsequence sums*.
  SIAM J. Discrete Math. (1996), 173-177.
- [Fr93] Freud, R., *Adding numbers - on a problem of P. Erdős*. James Cook Mathematical
  Notes (1993), 6199-6202.
-/

open Filter

namespace Erdos867

/-- A finite set of naturals $A=\{a_1<\cdots<a_t\}$ is *consecutive-sum-free* if it has no
solutions to $a_i+a_{i+1}+\cdots+a_j\in A$ with $i<j$; equivalently, whenever an interval
$[m,n]$ contains at least two elements of $A$, the sum of the elements of $A$ lying in
$[m,n]$ is not itself an element of $A$. -/
def ConsecutiveSumFree (A : Finset ℕ) : Prop :=
  ∀ m n : ℕ, 2 ≤ (Finset.Icc m n ∩ A).card → (∑ a ∈ Finset.Icc m n ∩ A, a) ∉ A

/--
Is it true that if $A=\{a_1<\cdots <a_t\}\subseteq \{1,\ldots,N\}$ has no solutions to
$$a_i+a_{i+1}+\cdots+a_j\in A$$
then
$$\lvert A\rvert \leq \frac{N}{2}+O(1)?$$

In fact this problem is false. Freud [Fr93] constructed a sequence with density $\geq 19/36$.
The current best bounds are due to Coppersmith and Phillips [CoPh96], who prove that the
maximal size of such an $A$ satisfies
$$\frac{13}{24}N -O(1)\leq \lvert A\rvert \leq \left(\frac{2}{3}-\frac{1}{512}\right)N+\log N.$$
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 5 11, formal_proof using lean4 at "https://github.com/plby/lean-proofs/blob/main/src/v4.29.1/ErdosProblems/Erdos867.lean"]
theorem erdos_867 : answer(False) ↔
    ∃ C : ℝ, ∀ N : ℕ, ∀ A ⊆ Finset.Icc 1 N, ConsecutiveSumFree A →
      (A.card : ℝ) ≤ (N : ℝ) / 2 + C := by
  sorry

/--
Taking $A=(N/2,N]\cap \mathbb{N}$ shows $\lvert A\rvert \geq N/2-O(1)$ is possible.
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 5 11]
theorem erdos_867.variants.lower_bound :
    ∃ C : ℝ, ∀ N : ℕ, ∃ A ⊆ Finset.Icc 1 N, ConsecutiveSumFree A ∧
      ((N : ℝ) / 2 - C ≤ (A.card : ℝ)) := by
  sorry

/--
Adenwalla has observed that
$$\lvert A\rvert \leq (\tfrac{2}{3}+o(1))N.$$
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 5 11]
theorem erdos_867.variants.adenwalla (ε : ℝ) (hε : 0 < ε) :
    ∀ᶠ N : ℕ in atTop, ∀ A ⊆ Finset.Icc 1 N, ConsecutiveSumFree A →
      (A.card : ℝ) ≤ (2 / 3 + ε) * (N : ℝ) := by
  sorry

/--
Freud [Fr93] constructed a sequence with density $\geq 19/36$.
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 5 11]
theorem erdos_867.variants.freud :
    ∀ ε : ℝ, 0 < ε → ∀ᶠ N : ℕ in atTop, ∃ A ⊆ Finset.Icc 1 N, ConsecutiveSumFree A ∧
      (((19 / 36 : ℝ) - ε) * (N : ℝ) ≤ (A.card : ℝ)) := by
  sorry

/--
The current best bounds are due to Coppersmith and Phillips [CoPh96], who prove that the
maximal size of such an $A$ satisfies
$$\frac{13}{24}N -O(1)\leq \lvert A\rvert.$$
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 5 11]
theorem erdos_867.variants.coppersmith_phillips_lower_bound :
    ∃ C : ℝ, ∀ N : ℕ, ∃ A ⊆ Finset.Icc 1 N, ConsecutiveSumFree A ∧
      ((13 / 24 : ℝ) * (N : ℝ) - C ≤ (A.card : ℝ)) := by
  sorry

/--
The current best bounds are due to Coppersmith and Phillips [CoPh96], who prove that the
maximal size of such an $A$ satisfies
$$\lvert A\rvert \leq \left(\frac{2}{3}-\frac{1}{512}\right)N+\log N.$$
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 5 11]
theorem erdos_867.variants.coppersmith_phillips_upper_bound :
    ∀ᶠ N : ℕ in atTop, ∀ A ⊆ Finset.Icc 1 N, ConsecutiveSumFree A →
      (A.card : ℝ) ≤ (2 / 3 - 1 / 512) * (N : ℝ) + Real.log (N : ℝ) := by
  sorry

end Erdos867

reformulations.difference: Uses intersections with intervals of values and a cardinality-at-least-two condition instead of consecutive indices and the source's equation a_i + ⋯ + a_j = a_k with i < j < k.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: Every nonempty intersection A ∩ [m,n] is a consecutive block of the increasing enumeration of A. Conversely, the block from a_i through a_j is A ∩ [a_i,a_j], and it contains at least two elements exactly when i < j. Under the positivity supplied by A ⊆ Icc 1 N, that block's sum exceeds a_j, so membership in A automatically gives an index k > j. Proved both the indexed-block equivalence and the positive, ordered-index version in /workspace/review/equivalence.lean (Review867.interval_iff_primary), using only standard axioms.

could_not_verify: Erdos867.erdos_867 — Could not independently confirm the current webpage's exact question and remarks: https://www.erdosproblems.com/867 and its forum returned Cloudflare challenges despite descriptive User-Agent headers. The accessible Coppersmith–Phillips abstract quotes the earlier N/2 + 1 question, so it alone does not verify that the cited webpage poses precisely the N/2 + O(1) version. The disproof of the Lean statement itself was kernel-checked.

Erdos867.erdos_867.variants.adenwalla — The webpage's Adenwalla remark was inaccessible. The epsilon/eventual formulation correctly expresses the docstring's (2/3 + o(1))N bound and is consistent with the stronger simple upper bound in the Coppersmith–Phillips abstract, but the exact attributed source claim could not be cross-checked.

Erdos867.erdos_867.variants.coppersmith_phillips_upper_bound — The full SIAM paper was blocked; only its abstract was accessible through Crossref and IBM. The abstract confirms (2/3 − 1/512)N + log N but does not specify the logarithm base or precise finite-N scope. Thus the choice of Real.log could not be fully verified against the paper's conventions; no logarithm-base defect is asserted.
review.notes: No confirmed mathematical defects or status mismatches. All declarations were inspected, with source-access limitations recorded below. The independent status database records problem 867 as disproved and formalized in Lean, matching the file. In a scratch copy, the linked proof compiled after updating one renamed Mathlib lemma; an added bridge proves the repository's exact real-constant statement with axioms only [propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound]. Independently proved the elementary lower bound with C = 0 and the equivalence of all-N versus eventual uniform O(1) bounds. Boundary tests and exhaustive checks through N = 12 passed. Freud's original 1993 paper was not obtained; its quantitative claim was checked against the Coppersmith–Phillips abstract and the linked construction. Detailed checks and artifacts are in /workspace/review/review-notes.md. No repository files were edited.
